headline: EU Regulatory Updates: CSRD, Green Claims, and Supply Chain Risks
summary: Germany has finalised its CSRD transposition negotiations, preparing the ground for your 2027 reporting obligations. Meanwhile, the EU's ban on vague green claims has entered into force, and discussions on extending CBAM to finished goods are intensifying. You must also monitor labor risks in China and prepare for upcoming deforestation rules.

items.title: German CSRD Transposition Negotiations Concluded
items.what: The German SPD announced that negotiations on the national CSRD transposition law are complete, clearing the path for final legislative adoption.
items.meaning: As a listed EU brand with over 1,000 employees, you will fall under the CSRD scope starting financial year 2027. German implementation details are now finalised.
items.action: Review the final German draft to align your 2027 reporting preparation with specific national requirements.

sources.title: CSRD-Umsetzungsgesetz: SPD sieht Verhandlungen als abgeschlossen

items.title: EU Ban on Vague Green Claims Enters into Force
items.what: The EU ban on vague environmental claims has officially entered into force, targeting greenwashing practices across consumer products.
items.meaning: Your consumer-facing marketing for power tools and garden equipment must avoid unsubstantiated claims like 'eco-friendly' or 'green' without detailed proof.
items.action: Audit all product packaging, manuals, and marketing materials to remove or substantiate generic environmental claims.

sources.title: Goodbye greenwashing? EU ban on vague claims comes into force

items.title: Proposed CBAM Extension to Downstream Products
items.what: Industry associations and the European Parliament are debating proposals to extend the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism to finished and semi-finished downstream products.
items.meaning: While you currently import finished goods exempt from CBAM, a downstream extension would subject your steel- and aluminium-heavy power tools to carbon tariffs.
items.action: Monitor these policy debates and assess the carbon intensity of your suppliers' manufacturing processes.

sources.title: Joint statement on the proposed downstream extension of the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)
European Parliament Backs Tougher, Wider-Reaching Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism
CLEPA joins call for workable CBAM rules that protect the entire automotive value chain
sources.origin: CLEPA | European Association of Automotive Suppliers

items.title: Chinese Workers File Overtime Complaints to EU
items.what: Chinese factory workers have submitted complaints to the EU regarding severe overtime, highlighting systemic labor risks in Chinese manufacturing sectors.
items.meaning: With 200 suppliers in mainland China, your brand faces heightened reputational and regulatory scrutiny regarding working hours and labor conditions.
items.action: Engage with Chinese suppliers to audit working hours and ensure compliance with local labor laws.

sources.title: Brutale Überstunden-Kultur: Chinas Arbeiter beschweren sich bei der EU

items.title: EU Updates EUDR Customs Codes as Penalties Formulate
items.what: The EU updated customs codes and Information System guidance for the Deforestation Regulation, while Germany and Ireland proposed severe non-compliance penalties.
items.meaning: If your packaging or product components contain wood or paper, you must comply with EUDR. National laws propose heavy fines and prison terms.
items.action: Verify if any imported packaging or product elements trigger EUDR, and prepare due diligence statements.

sources.title: EU updates EUDR customs codes and Information System guidance ahead of December application

Companies that fail to meet Ireland's Deforestation Regulations could be fined up to 10 million euros
